assumptions.title: Eleveld parameter set: arterial, ke0 0.146 x (W/70)^-0.25
assumptions.body: Pumps and open simulators implement the arterial Eleveld set [eleveld2018]. The user's nine golden values match the arterial set to within 0.5% (venous gives about a third of the bolus). Whether the Space Plus uses arterial or venous parameters is not publicly documented: test question Q8.

assumptions.title: Opioid flag
assumptions.body: "Opioid on" means opioids present: V3 and CL are multiplied by exp(theta x age), uncentred, so the published reference values hold only without opioids [eleveld2018] [vandemoortele2022]. The app defaults to opioid on. The Space Plus default is unknown (Q5).

assumptions.title: Effect-site bolus: peak Ce equals target
assumptions.body: The induction bolus is the dose whose peak Ce equals the target [shafer1992]. The matcher treats it as instantaneous by default, which reproduces the golden values; Settings can run it at the pump's maximum rate instead. No cap on the plasma overshoot is applied, because none is documented for the Space Plus [vanpoucke2004].

assumptions.title: Matched target
assumptions.body: Because the models are linear, the matched target on model B is the bolus on model A divided by model B's bolus per unit target. It matches the induction bolus only; maintenance rates and clinical effect differ, and published loss-of-consciousness Ce values differ about threefold between models [introna2026b] [linassi2023].

assumptions.title: Schnider ke0 fixed at 0.456
assumptions.body: The emulator uses a fixed ke0 of 0.456 /min (time to peak about 1.5 min) [schnider1999]. Some pumps instead derive ke0 per patient from a 1.6 min time to peak [absalom2009]; the Space Plus is reported, weakly, to use the fixed value (Q4).

assumptions.title: Marsh ke0
assumptions.body: Selectable: 0.26 /min (original, time to peak about 3.9 min) or 1.2 /min (modified, about 1.6 min) [marsh1991] [struys2000]. Weak evidence suggests the Space Plus offers Marsh in plasma mode only, with 0.26 listed (Q3).

assumptions.title: James LBM limit
assumptions.body: James LBM peaks at BMI 43.0 (male) and 36.1 (female) and then falls, so Schnider clearance becomes wrong in obesity [james1976]. The app warns from 80% of the peak weight and flags weights past it. Pump BMI cut-offs (often 42 male, 35 female) are not confirmed for any named pump.

assumptions.title: Reported Space Plus BMI above 30 behaviour
assumptions.body: Reported: above BMI 30 the Space Plus Eleveld model uses an adjusted weight in place of total body weight [milliet2025] [anzca2025]. The app's BMI above 30 mode substitutes Servin's adjusted weight, IBW (Devine) + 0.4 x excess [servin1993], for weight in every Eleveld covariate. This reproduces the published index case (163 mg vs the pump's 162 mg; total body weight gives 191 mg vs TivaTrainer's 192 mg). Which covariates the pump changes, whether maintenance is affected, the affected software versions, and the fix status are not published (Q1, Q7).

assumptions.title: Pump settings
assumptions.body: Defaults: propofol 1%, maximum rate 1200 mL/h, rate recomputed every 10 s. A datasheet lists up to 1800 mL/h for the Space plus Perfusor [bbraun]; the update interval is not documented. A lower target stops the infusion until the predicted level falls (Q11, Q12).

assumptions.title: Solver
assumptions.body: Exact: analytic poly-exponential in the app, matrix exponential in the Python oracle; they agree to better than 1e-6 relative. Piecewise-constant infusion, no numerical integration.

assumptions.title: Validity ranges
assumptions.body: Warnings use the source data ranges: Eleveld up to 88 y and 160 kg [eleveld2018]; Schnider volunteers 26-81 y, 44-123 kg [schnider1998]. Pump input limits are not confirmed (Q6).
